records.title: Post decompression shock (a case report)
records.locator: Case History, pp. 10–13, and Discussion, pp. 13–14 (PDF pp. 2–6)
records.evidence_note: An Indian Air Force aircrew member undergoing a preconversion altitude chamber test in New Delhi developed symptoms at altitude and circulatory collapse after temporary improvement. Hospital discharge listed DCS. The author discussed pulmonary vascular air embolism as a possible mechanism without confirmation. The recorded description supports a historical author-diagnosed case, with no modern diagnostic reassessment. Subject was undergoing the test and a medical observer was separately described.

observations.locator: Case History and discharge diagnosis, pp. 10–13
observations.note: Chamber testing preceded the conversion course. The author discusses mechanism uncertainty. The report gives no exposed population or staff comparator.

records.title: Refresher altitude chamber training for aircrew: A questionnaire feedback survey
records.locator: Abstract, p. 1, Discussion, p. 11, and reference 5, pp. 12–13
records.evidence_note: The questionnaire covers one center from January 2002 to December 2003. The Discussion describes a separate database of chamber side effects with no DCS over six years. Reference 5 gives the 1998–2003 surveillance period and Sun City presentation. The questionnaires are from a different sampling frame. Staff roles, total six-year exposures, case definition and follow-up are unavailable.

observations.locator: Joshi and Thakur 2005, Discussion, p. 11 and reference 5
observations.note: The six-year data are cited secondhand. The 142 feedback questionnaires and 74 returns at No. 1 AMTC apply to a separate 2002–2003 survey and cannot be used as its denominator.

records.title: A retrospective analysis of altitude chamber training protocols and the adverse effects at Aero Medical Training Centers in the Indian Air Force: 1998–2003
records.event: 52nd International Congress on Aviation and Space Medicine, Sun City, South Africa
records.evidence_note: Joshi and Thakur give the exact author, title, period, meeting and presentation date. Kasture et al. corroborate the title and meeting in reference 9. Searches did not locate a copy of the abstract, paper or original tables, and the exposure denominators remain unknown.

records.title: Women in Fighter Cockpit: A Review with IAF Perspective
records.evidence_note: The narrative claims no DCI during IAF chamber training and gives no period, denominator, ascertainment method, role assignment or supporting surveillance citation for that statement. It is not extracted as a quantified cohort. The 1957 paper reports a much earlier case during a preconversion test and should be considered when interpreting the scope of this general statement.

note: Checked the published barotrauma table, its preliminary proceedings report, and the cited departmental study.

records.evidence_note: The issue carries a Winter 2025 label and the publisher and PDF show online publication in September 2026. Grades were abstracted from records. The report lacks event altitude and delayed barotrauma follow-up, and does not ascertain DCS. Counts by service partition the same total.

records.title: Incidence of otitic barotrauma during decompression test in Indian armed forces between 2019 to 2022
records.evidence_note: The abstract gives the same period, site, 639 volunteers, 30 unfit, 609 exposed and 40 events as the full report. The 7.1% reference to an earlier study differs from 7.4% in the final paper. No second case count is entered for this preliminary report.

records.title: Incidence of Barotrauma during Decompression Test for Combat Free Fall Trainees with Modified Protocol
records.locator: Sharma et al., reference 4, and Raghunandan and Mohapatra, reference 6
records.evidence_note: Raghunandan and Mohapatra identify the IAM project as unpublished. Sharma et al. specify June 2015 to October 2018 and cite a 7.4% otitic barotrauma rate. The conference version quotes 7.1%. Original counts and exposure totals remain unavailable.

records.title: A paradigm approach toward predicting barotrauma
records.evidence_note: The publication identifies the earlier IAM cohort as an unpublished departmental project and quotes a 7.1% rate. It supplies no underlying case or exposure totals.

records.title: Decompression chamber runs for screening and training of HALO paratroopers and training of fighter aircrew
records.evidence_note: The paper separates the actual descent cohort from a simulated ear-clearance protocol experiment with repeated measures in 50 paratroopers. The recorded outcomes are ear symptoms and middle-ear findings.

note: Verified when an author explicitly reported zero DCS and when papers reported only hypoxia outcomes.

records.title: Hypoxia signature: A useful tool for hypoxia recognition among aircrew
records.evidence_note: The study measured hypoxia symptoms, heart rate and oxygen saturation over three exposures in 22 healthy volunteers. It provides an independent citation of the 2004 IAF surveillance report without additional DCS numbers.

records.title: Hypobaric and Normobaric Hypoxia Training in Aircrew: A Comparative Study
records.evidence_note: Both exposures were tested in the same 23 people. The measured outcomes were subjective hypoxia symptoms, physiology and psychomotor performance. The paper mentions DCS as a training hazard but provides no DCS ascertainment or counts.

records.title: Combined altitude depleted oxygen vis-à-vis hypobaric hypoxia: Efficacy in hypoxia indoctrination
records.evidence_note: The paper compares acute hypoxia responses and psychomotor measures. Its general DCS safety statements do not supply an observed DCS case count or a staff comparison.

records.title: Psychophysiological Responses of Pilots in Hypoxia Training at 7000 and 7500 m
records.evidence_note: Methods specify random equal assignment of the 66 pilots to two independent groups. The Discussion reports zero DCS during the 7000 m experiment. Its rate comparison comes from prior populations, not a DCS count for the 7500 m experimental group. The paper gives no systematic delayed follow-up or staff outcome data.

observations.group: Pilots assigned to the 7000 m experimental exposure
observations.note: Equal allocation of 66 pilots implies 33 at each altitude. The zero is explicitly reported during the 7000 m session only. The opposite arm has no explicit DCS count in the article.
